protocol.name: beize_shell_v1

description.summary: what Beize's shell knows of the windows (ADR 0028 §1)

protocol.description:
The compositor tells Beize's shell which windows there are – their app, title and state – and does what the shell asks of them: the dock lists the running apps and brings their windows back, the menu bar names the active app. Modelled on ext-foreign-toplevel-list-v1 (the list) and wlr-foreign-toplevel-management (what the shell asks).
The shell hears the appearance, light or dark, that tints the glass (beize-app-v1).
Only the shell is offered the global; the compositor knows it by its unit (os/beize-compositor, trust.rs). Both ends live in Beize's repository and change together: until a version of Beize promises otherwise, the protocol grows without new versions.

interface.name: beize_shell_v1
interface.description: On bind the compositor tells the appearance, then announces every window there is, in the order they opened, then each new one when it first shows.

event.name: appearance
event.description: The system's appearance, and again when it changes: the glass's tint follows it, the shell's content should too.

event.name: menu_bar_backdrop

description.summary: how light it is behind the menu bar

event.description: The menu bar has no background (ADR 0028 §3): what lies behind it is the background, which the compositor measures there – once known, and again when the background changes. The bar's ink follows it.

request.name: ready
request.description: Sent once, after the shell committed the first content of each panel it shows from the start. The desktop appears in one piece (ADR 0028 §6): the compositor shows it only now, or without the shell if it ends before or hangs. A shell started after one failed replaces with it the panels the compositor kept of the old.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The windows announced so far stay valid until destroyed.

request.name: set_appearance
request.description: The user chose the appearance (the control center): the compositor keeps it, tints the glass and the background for it and tells every instance (appearance).

event.name: window
event.description: A window is there: its app_id, title and state follow, then done.

event.name: switcher_entry
event.description: The windows of a switcher about to show, in its order. A window closed meanwhile leaves it with its closed event.

event.name: switcher_show
event.description: Its entries are complete; it has this room at most.

request.name: clear_thumbnails

description.summary: no windows' pictures on a surface

request.description: None of the pictures asked for before (beize_window_v1.show_thumbnail) with the surface's next commit.

interface.name: beize_window_v1
interface.description: Its properties come as events, each set of changes ended by done.

entry.name: active
entry.summary: it has the keyboard; at most one window is active

entry.name: minimized
entry.summary: it is minimized: not on the screen

event.name: app_id
event.description: The app's id (xdg_toplevel.app_id): the name of its desktop file without ".desktop". Empty if the app named none.

description.summary: the changes before it belong together
the window's menus are described anew
a menu after the last, by its title
a command at the end of the last menu
a line at the end of the last menu

event.name: closed
event.description: No more events come; the shell destroys the object.

request.name: activate

description.summary: bring the window to the front

request.description: Shows it again if it is minimized, raises it and gives it the keyboard.

description.summary: the user chose a command of the window's menus
choose it in the switcher, which ends

request.name: show_thumbnail

description.summary: the window's live picture on a surface

request.description: As DwmRegisterThumbnail: the compositor draws the window, scaled down to fit the rectangle in the shell's surface and centred, in front of it. Double-buffered: applies with the surface's next commit.

request.name: close
request.description: As its own close button does (xdg_toplevel.close): the app decides.
